full_judgment:
A. M. Mahmudur Rahman, J.: This Miscellaneous Appeal is against the Judgment and order dated July, 25,1974 passed by the learned Subordinate Judge, Khulna, dismissing the Miscellaneous Case No. 282 of 1972 instituted upon an application under Or. 9 R.13 C.P.C. 

 2. The Respondent 1 Instituted Money Suit No. 109 of 1970 against the Appellant. The suit was decreed ex-parte on July 14, 1972. Thereupon the aforesaid Miscellaneous Case was started. The learned Judge, on contest, dismissed the Miscellaneous Case leading to filing the present Miscellaneous Appeal. 

 3. Mr. Shahabuddin Ahmed seriously contends that the remark of the learned Judge on the demenanour of P.W.1 that the petitioner P.W. 1 at the time of this deposition was Speaking in a manner as if he was suppressing the real truth "under Or. 18 R.12 C.P.C. is not objective. He submits that the Court has power to make observation about the demeanour of a witness but such observation must not be subjective but must be based on objective materials. According to him, the observation is not based, in the instant case, on material object or in otherwise the observation is not objective but subjective. In support of his contention, he relied upon the decision in the case of Pothan Chandy Vs. Ouseph Kochousepth reported in A.I.R. 1951, Tri-Cochin 12. Mr. Shahabuddin Ahmed referred me to paragraph 3 of the Judgment. The observation made at paragraph 3 of the decision relied upon by Mr. Ahmed does not support the contention of Mr. Shahabuddin Ahmed. In the instant case the remark was made in the Judgment itself and not after closing the evidence and after reading over the same and signed by the Judge. In the aforesaid case, the application arose out of an application under Section 24 C.P.C. on the ground that the Judge after signing the deposition remarked this witness strike me as unscrupulous." In that Judgment the remark was made by the learned Judge after signing the deposition sheet unlike the present one where the remark was made in the body of the Judgment. Or. 18. R. 12 C.P.C. does not disentitled a Judge to make a remark on the demeanour of witness in the Judgment as has been done here. Therefore, on facts of this case, the principle laid down in Pothan Chandy has little application to the facts of the instant case. The decision does not help Mr. Shahabuddin as the remark was made in that case after closing the evidence and not in the body of the Judgment. The Court is not permitted to make remark about the demeanour of a witness after examination of the witness and after the deposition was read over and signed, but premises a Judge to make such remark in the body of the Judgment under Or. 18. r. 12. C.P.C. 

 4. Now, let us see on merit, how far the Appellant was successful to prove his case. In other words, whether he was prevented from sufficient cause in not appearing at the time of hearing of the suit. On a careful perusal of the Judgment and order impugned, it appears that the learned Judge, after consideration of the evidence on record, came to the finding that the Petitioner willfully avoided to appear. This finding is based on the statement of the Petitioner himself who stated that he came to know about the ex-parte decree from one of the staffs of the Bank on 7.8.72, but he could not disclose the same to the employee when he was given such information. The learned Judge also noted material discrepancy in the statement of P.W.1 (Plaintiff) and his brother P.W.2 so far as handing over the papers and the power to the learned Advocate Mr. Delwar Hossain is concerned. It appears that the Petitioner stated in the petition under Or. 9 r. 13 C.P.C. that he handed over the power to Mr. Delwar Hossain, Advocate, without mentioning the year. He has also stated that he sent the papers through Biman from Dhaka. It is not understood how and why he handed over the power to Mr. Delwar Hossain through his brother when he sent the same through Biman. This contradiction was taken into consideration by the Court of Appeal in disbelieving the statement of P.W.1. In this regard Mr. Shahabuddin Ahmed submits that during those troubled days, the power was sent per Avon to Mr. Delwar Hossain, but he was not at Khulna at that time and till 1973. He submits pointing to this aspect that the Court should take a lenient view to set aside an ex-parte decree which resulted from no laches or fault of the Advocate of the litigant. Thus, Court sometimes takes such view, but each case is to be decided on its peculiar facts and circumstances. In this case, in view of the findings of the Court, I am of the opinion that the findings are based on cogent reason on evidence and the learned Judge rightly arrived at a finding that the Appellant willfully avoided to appear when the suit was taken up for hearing. The Judgment impugned does not call for any interference.
